verdict.rationale: Lago documents its own outbound webhooks with reliability features: HMAC signatures, automatic retries on non-2xx responses or network errors (3 attempts), and a log for inspecting and retrying events. The pack never lists which subscription events fire, so coverage of renewal, upgrade, payment failure and cancellation is unproven. Missing for 10: an enumerated list of subscription lifecycle webhook event types (renewal, upgrade/downgrade, payment failure, cancellation), registration or endpoint configuration details, and independent or hands-on corroboration of delivery reliability.

support.subject: As a developer, every subscription state change — renewal, upgrade, payment failure, cancellation — emits a webhook or event my systems can act on reliably

citations.quote: If you return an error (other than a 2xx's HTTP response) or if there is a network issue, the webhook will be sent again. Lago will try to send the webhook 3 times.
This allows you to take a closer look at the generated events, detect possible errors, and retry them.
The second is `HMAC`, which features a shorter payload header and no size restrictions.
